verdict.rationale: On the ACP path, the delegated credential is a one-time-use Braintree token rather than raw card data. It is bound to the merchant ID and carries configurable amount and time restrictions. The UCP path likewise passes a single-use Braintree token. However, these are documented from the merchant's integration side, and the restrictions are configured by the merchant, not issued or scoped by the user for their own agent. Missing for 10: user-facing issuance of scoped credentials to the user's own agent, user-set spending limits and expiry, multi-merchant restriction controls, and hands-on or independent corroboration.
